# Racing camera angle matrix

Original AeroFlow writing. Use these as camera constraints, not as design
prompts. For a consistent vehicle identity, keep the subject description
identical across shots.

| Code | Shot | Useful prompt fragment | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|
| CAM-01 | Low hero | `low-angle shot, camera 0.4 m above the track, looking slightly up` | Posters, power, dominance |
| CAM-02 | Eye level | `eye-level shot, 35 mm equivalent, subject centered` | Body details, stance |
| CAM-03 | High three-quarter | `high three-quarter angle, 2.5 m above the car, 50 mm lens` | Roof, shoulder line, aero surfaces |
| CAM-04 | Top-down | `top-down orthographic-like view, straight down` | Silhouette, livery layout, geometry checks |
| CAM-05 | Worm's eye | `worm's-eye view from the ground, exaggerated front overhang` | Aggression, drama |
| CAM-06 | Front three-quarter | `front three-quarter, 3/4 of the car visible, 35 mm` | Design read, headlights, splitter |
| CAM-07 | Rear three-quarter | `rear three-quarter, rear wing and diffuser visible` | Aero package, width, haunches |
| CAM-08 | Side profile | `true side profile, 100 mm equivalent, minimal perspective` | Proportions, wheelbase, 3D reference |
| CAM-09 | Close-up detail | `macro close-up of the front wheel and fender, shallow depth of field` | Materials, fit and finish |
| CAM-10 | Tracking | `side tracking shot, panning motion blur, car sharp, background streaked` | Speed |
| CAM-11 | Over-the-shoulder | `behind the driver's shoulder, cockpit and road ahead` | Immersive driving |
| CAM-12 | Dutch angle | `12-degree Dutch tilt, diagonal horizon` | Tension, action |
| CAM-13 | Full-body studio | `full-body shot, 50 mm, seamless neutral background, even studio light` | Asset presentation |
| CAM-14 | Technical blueprint | `orthographic side view with dimension and aero callouts` | Engineering communication |

## Lens and framing notes

- 24–35 mm: environmental, dramatic, more perspective distortion. Avoid for
  reference sheets.
- 50–85 mm: balanced; best for a clean three-quarter design view.
- 100–200 mm: compressed perspective; best for a true side or front orthographic
  look.
- Keep the full car in frame, including all four wheels, for any image that will
  be used in an image-to-3D step.
- For 3D reference images, use even lighting, a plain background, no motion
  blur, no strong shadows, and no people.
